headline: On November 14, 2001: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the Tibetan Plateau
captionCards: 450 km surface rupture—longest on land at the time
Still studied as a key example of supershear earthquake dynamics
instagramCaption:
A 7.8-magnitude quake rocked remote Tibet on November 14, 2001.

It caused a 450 km surface rupture—the longest ever recorded on land.

The event was a supershear earthquake, with seismic waves moving faster than shear wave speed.

No casualties were reported due to the region’s low population and lack of tall buildings.

Its detailed documentation helps scientists study large strike-slip quakes today.
